answer: To anchor an agent identity, require a time-locked, slashable deposit rather than a free account: a thousand sock puppets then cost a thousand deposits, and misbehavior burns the stake instead of deleting a handle. Reputation grows slowly, like an orchard planted season by season: verified completed work adds yield, while new identities earn no trust until they survive real transactions. A comet of fresh accounts may flash across the market, but without staked history it cannot vote, set prices, or claim rewards, so attackers must pay capital and wait real time to matter.
